title: The post charge-off sale harness pack for the debt sale handover is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 and §R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 43 (lines 2896 to 2899 and 2949 to 2950) and the S6 block at lines 1397 to 1403; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 lines 1555 and 1815 to 1819; legacy RWB-E6-028 sections Data, Endpoints, Screen and states and Test cases; ownership.json api and tables
description: (a) No source read gives the harness environment and its base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic case keys beyond the RW-YYYY-NNNNNN form (DF-CAS-002), the synthetic write-off and lot keys, the population size, the two inside-limit and one above-limit amounts, the write-off committee limit itself, the business date, the evidence format and retention, or the pass or fail gate. The legacy story names no synthetic key, no amount, no limit and no business date, and the Architecture v5 slides give the service, the topic and the queue only. (b) No source read publishes a write-off read or a write-off sale operation. ownership.json gives POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision to S7 and nothing else on the write-off, so the population has to be identified through the P3 case read, the P7 decision log and DP09 Debt sale read through P1, and the handover has to be driven by S6's own published lot operation POST /debt-sale-lots with GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId} as its read, which is what Architecture v5 line 1397 names as GET/POST /lots.
evidence: Read and confirmed: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 2896 to 2899 (S5, S6 and S7 service rows) and 2949 to 2950 (events 23 LotAwarded and 24 WriteOffApproved), lines 1397 to 1403 (S6 REST GET/POST /lots, POST /lots/{id}/award, DebtSaleWorkflow saga pivot = transfer); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 lines 1555 and 1815 to 1819 (point of no return and strict mode); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 342, 343, 344, 346, 351, 360, 362 and 363; legacy RWB-E6-028 lines 10889 to 10908 and 10926 to 10935, which name no synthetic key, amount, limit or business date; ownership.json api entries for POST /write-offs/{writeOffId}/committee-decision, GET /approvals, POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve, GET /decision-log, GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}, POST /debt-sale-lots, GET /data-products/{productCode}/records and GET /me/session, and tables write_off (S7), debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account (S6), recovery_case (P3), decision_log_entry, approval and rule_row (P7)
proposed: Agree the fixture layout, the synthetic case, write-off and lot keys, the amount set and the write-off committee limit, the business date, the evidence retention and the gate at the wave 4 entry check, and hold each of them as configuration; record that the write-off read and the write-off sale operation do not exist, so the population is asserted through the case read, the decision log and DP09 and the handover is driven by S6's published lot operation

title: Partner-onboarding integration harness: environment, fixture keys, terms fixture, business date, evidence and gate are not specified, the Ownership Map publishes no partner create or panel-change operation, and neither the InstructionRequest shape nor the right required to onboard is published
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md §R5.5, §R7.3 and §R9; _work/msr/wp/B-ITG-W4-05.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E6-029 lines 11820-11899
description: RWB-ITG-E6029-ITG needs four things no source gives. (a) The SIT environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and contract keys, the terms fixture that carries the fee schedule version, the service levels and the scope, the business date, the evidence format and its retention, and the pass or fail gate at the wave entry check. (b) The Ownership Map publishes GET /partners and GET /partner/instructions but no partner create and no panel-change operation, so the onboarding write cannot be driven through a published operation: it is RWB-S9-E6029-APP's own path and is observed here only through the published read, DP08 and the decision log, and the harness must never compose a partner endpoint. (c) The InstructionRequest body of POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions is named in TSD S9 appendix T-A but not shaped anywhere in the extracted sources, and no source states which capability-area right the onboarding itself needs; the TSD RBAC matrix gives every listed role at least Partner portal R, so AC6 is proved on a negative session fixture rather than on a role that lacks the right. One placeholder is therefore used in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8, 13 and 15.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E6-029 (User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, lines 11820-11899) names the two partner reads, the partner, decision_log_entry and rule_row entities with their DF ranges, SCR-34 and SCR-35, one permission-check row and TC-E6-029-01 to TC-E6-029-04, and states no environment, fixture, key scheme, terms fixture, business date, evidence format or gate; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 line 134 (FEAT-PRM-01, prerequisite FEAT-OCC-13) and Business Requirements Program v4 lines 430, 431 and 437 (REQ-S9-001, REQ-S9-002, REQ-S9-008) give the outcome and no harness detail; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 361, 362, 429, 430, 431, 433 and 449 (R-WO-30, R-WO-31, R-UNI-25, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-27, R-UNI-29, R-UNI-45) give the placement and recall rules and no harness configuration; FSD S9 Partner management v3 lines 89-170 gives the step table, VR-S9-001-1, BR-S9-001, the field catalogue, the two roles and AC-EXC-S9-001-01 and AC-EXC-S9-001-02, and names no onboarding operation; TSD S9 Partner management v2 lines 197-277 lists API-S9-001 to API-S9-006 and names InstructionRequest as the request body of API-S9-002 without defining it, and lines 130-165 gives Partner portal R to RW-CASEOWN and every other listed role; ownership.json holds S9 for GET /partners, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions, P1 for GET /data-products/{productCode}/records, P3 for GET /cases/{caseId}, P7 for GET /decision-log and P4 for GET /me/session, and holds no partner create or panel-change operation; Arch v5 lines 1245-1256 and 1270-1272, line 2891 and slide 43 rows 20 and 21 (lines 2946 and 2947) give the contract, the schema and the events and no harness artefact; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 25 lines 1663-1755 gives step 1 and the clocks and no harness; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3 lists the fill order and none of its sources holds these values.
area: Integration harness configuration and contract coverage
proposed: Agree at the wave 4 entry check the SIT base hosts, the fixture layout and the synthetic partner and contract key scheme, the terms fixture with its fee schedule version, service levels and scope, the business date, the evidence format and retention and the pass or fail gate, and record them in the harness README; publish the InstructionRequest shape in RWB-S9-E6029-CON and state the capability-area right the onboarding needs, or confirm that the onboarding is proved through the published reads with a negative session fixture for the refusal; the fixture values stay data and no business value is hard-coded.

title: Partner panel and fee-schedule harness: environment, fixture versions, evidence and gate are not specified, and no panel-version or fee-schedule load operation is published
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R7.3 and R9; _work/msr/wp/B-ITG-W4-05.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E6-030 lines 11901-11979; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: RWB-ITG-E6030-ITG needs three things no source gives. (a) The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and case keys, the panel version and the two fee schedule versions, the service levels by partner type, the business date and the next effective date, the evidence format and its retention, and the pass or fail gate at the wave entry check are all unpublished. (b) The Ownership Map publishes GET /partners and the partner-instruction operations of S9 but no panel-version or fee-schedule load operation and no parameter that carries either version, so the version load is RWB-S9-E6030-APP's and is observed here only through the published reads, the reference-data contract of P3 and the decision log. (c) The shape of a versioned reference load and its valid-from rule are published for rule packages and for lov_value (valid_from) but not for the partner panel or the fee schedule, so no field, endpoint or payload of a partner-panel version can be asserted.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E6-030 (User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, lines 11901-11979) names the partner, decision_log_entry, rule_row and lov_value entities, the two partner endpoints, SCR-34 and SCR-35, the permission checks, the three messages and TC-E6-030-01 to TC-E6-030-04, and states no environment, fixture, version, date, evidence format or gate; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 line 135 (FEAT-PRM-02, prerequisite FEAT-CWC-23) names the outcome only; Business Requirements Program v4 lines 430 and 433 (REQ-S9-001, REQ-S9-004) name the six points and the fee basis only; FSD S9 Partner management v3 A2.2 lines 173-255 gives the step table, VR-S9-002-1, BR-S9-002, the field catalogue and the two exception criteria and no version shape; TSD S9 Partner management v2 lines 63-106 give the partner and partner_instruction fields and lines 91-99 the four LOV blocks, with no version table; Architecture v5 lines 1245-1256 and 1270-1272 and slide 41 line 2891 give the contract, the event and the schema and no load operation; Temporal and Drools design slide 25 lines 1663-1755 gives the journey and the clocks, and lines 790-798 and 1901-1932 publish valid-from and the refused-load state for rule packages only; ownership.json lists GET /partners, POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions as S9's, GET /admin/lists/{listCode}, GET /admin/parameters and GET /admin/change-log as P3's, GET /decision-log as P7's and GET /me/session as P4's, and no version-load operation.
area: Integration harness configuration; partner panel and fee-schedule version contract
proposed: Agree at the wave 4 entry check: SIT and the base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partner and case keys, the panel version and the two fee schedule versions, the service levels, the business date and the next effective date, the evidence format and retention, and a gate in which a stub pass is never a real pass. Publish the panel-version and fee-schedule load operation, or state that the version in force is read only through the partner read and the decision entry, and publish the valid-from rule for a partner-panel version so the shape can be asserted.

title: Measured-return placement harness: environment, fixture and keys, scorecard version, measured-return values, freshness cut-off and gate are not specified, the map publishes no allocation or scorecard read, the InstructionRequest shape is not published, and the legacy endpoint table names R and U where the placement declares C
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md §R7.3 and §R9; _work/msr/wp/B-ITG-W4-05.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E6-031 lines 11983-12062; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2.md lines 197-244
description: RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG needs four sets of values no source gives. (a) The harness environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partners, cases and instruction keys, the scorecard version, the measured-return values that rank A first on business date 2027-04-30 and B first on the next business date, the capacity state of the three partners, the business date and the next business date, the freshness cut-off that decides that DP11 is stale, the evidence format and its retention, and the pass or fail gate at the wave entry check. (b) The Ownership Map publishes no allocation read and no scorecard read, so the pick can only be asserted through the instruction S9 issues, the measured return through DP08 and the score through DP11; the story must never invent an allocation endpoint to make the assertion cleaner. (c) The InstructionRequest body shape of API-S9-002 is not published, so the body the run sends is held in the fixture from S9's CON story and only the published PartnerInstruction response fields are asserted. (d) The legacy endpoint table of RWB-E6-031 names Partner portal R on GET /partner/instructions and Partner portal U on POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results, while the published placement operation POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions declares Partner portal C; the story follows the published matrix and records the legacy table as the earlier read and result paths.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E6-031 (User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, lines 11983-12062) names the feature, the data entities, two partner-portal endpoints, SCR-34 and SCR-35, the permission checks, three messages and TC-E6-031-01 to TC-E6-031-04, and states no environment, fixture, key scheme, scorecard version, measured-return value, capacity state, freshness cut-off, evidence format or gate. TSD S9 v2 lines 197-244 publish API-S9-002 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions with purpose 'Issue an instruction to a partner by rule', request InstructionRequest, response PartnerInstruction, right Partner portal C and an Idempotency-Key, and API-S9-003 GET /partner/instructions with right R, and publish no allocation list, no scorecard read and no InstructionRequest field list. ownership.json holds only S9 POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions, P1 GET /data-products/{productCode}/records and GET /data-products/freshness, P3 GET /cases/{caseId}, P7 GET /decision-log and P4 GET /me/session, and no allocation read. FSD S9 A2.3 (lines 257-326) gives the steps, VR-S9-003-1 with MSG-P1-001, BR-S9-003 and the roles, and no harness detail; Business Requirements Program v4 line 432 (REQ-S9-003) gives the rule; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 361 and 362 (R-WO-30, R-WO-31) give 'same day on the portal' and 'hold the placement' and define no cut-off; FSD P1 lines 290 and 293 give DP08 on change and DP11 daily at 08:00 and no stale threshold; Arch v5 slides 17 and 41 (lines 1245-1256, 1270-1272, 2891) and slide 43 row 20 (line 2946) give the contract and the event; Temporal design slide 25 (lines 1663-1755) gives the scorecard pick, the instruction and the clocks; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3 lists the fill order and none of its sources holds these values.
area: Integration harness configuration and published contract gaps for S9 allocation by measured return
proposed: Agree at the wave 4 entry check: SIT with the base hosts, the fixture layout and the synthetic partners PRT-SYN-0031-A, PRT-SYN-0031-B and PRT-SYN-0031-C with cases RW-2027-000831 and RW-2027-000832, the scorecard version, the measured-return values for business date 2027-04-30 and the next business date, the capacity state, the freshness cut-off, the evidence format and retention and a gate in which a stub pass is never a real pass; keep the pick asserted through the instruction, DP08 and DP11 and add no allocation endpoint; hold the InstructionRequest body in the fixture from S9's CON story; and read the placement right as Partner portal C per API-S9-002, with the legacy table's R and U recorded as the earlier read and result paths.

title: Partner allocation override harness: environment, fixture keys, reason code, evidence and gate are not specified; the map publishes no override operation and no reason field name or outside-panel refusal message
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md §R5.5, §R7.3 and §R9; _work/msr/wp/B-ITG-W4-05.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E6-032 lines 12066-12144; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S9 Partner management v2.md lines 197-244; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: RWB-ITG-E6032-ITG needs three sets of values that no source gives. (a) The SIT environment and base hosts, the fixture layout, the synthetic partners, case and instruction keys, the reason code and its text, the business date, the evidence format and its retention, and the pass or fail gate at the wave entry check. (b) The override has no published operation of its own: the Ownership Map and TSD S9 publish only POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions and GET /partner/instructions for S9, so the override rides on the published placement and the InstructionRequest and PartnerInstruction shapes are not published either, which leaves the request body to be held in the fixture from S9's CON story. (c) The reason field name is not published and the refusal message for a partner outside the panel is not specified at all, so the run asserts 409 and MSG-GEN-001 only where API-S9-002's published error list (401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503) and VR-S9-004-1 allow it, and invents no message. One placeholder is used in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8, 13 and 15.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E6-032 (User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, lines 12066-12144) gives the story, AC1 and AC2, the four data entities, two partner-portal endpoints, SCR-35 and SCR-34, the permission checks, three messages and TC-E6-032-01 to TC-E6-032-04, and states no environment, fixture, key scheme, reason code, evidence format or gate; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 line 137 (FEAT-PRM-04, prerequisite FEAT-PRM-03 at line 136) and Business Requirements Program v4 line 432 (REQ-S9-003) name the outcome and no harness detail; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 361, 362, 428, 430, 431, 433 and 449 (R-WO-30, R-WO-31, R-UNI-24, R-UNI-26, R-UNI-27, R-UNI-29, R-UNI-45) give the states and the correction pattern and no reason code; FSD S9 v3 A2.4 lines 328-408 gives VR-S9-004-1 with MSG-GEN-001 on 'Required field empty', BR-S9-004 and the field catalogue without naming the reason field, and the two exception criteria AC-EXC-S9-004-01 and AC-EXC-S9-004-02 without a message for an outside-panel partner; TSD S9 v2 lines 197-244 gives API-S9-002 as 'Issue an instruction to a partner by rule' with purpose, right C, Idempotency-Key and the six errors, and publishes neither the InstructionRequest shape nor a reason field; Arch v5 lines 1245-1256 and 1270-1272, slide 41 line 2891 and slide 43 row 20 line 2946 give the contract, the schema and the event and no harness; Temporal and Drools design slide 25 lines 1663-1755, line 1739, states 'Partner manager: overrides need a reason' and no field name; ownership.json names S9 as owner of both partner operations and of partner and partner_instruction, P3 of the case, P7 of the decision log and P4 of the session, and names no harness artefact; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3 lists the fill order and none of its sources holds these values.
area: Integration harness configuration and unpublished override contract detail
proposed: Agree at the wave 4 entry check: SIT and the base hosts, the fixture layout and the synthetic partners, case, instruction and reason keys, the evidence format and retention, and a gate in which a stub pass is never a real pass. Publish the InstructionRequest and PartnerInstruction shapes with S9's CON story and name the reason field and any outside-panel refusal message there; until then the harness holds the request in the fixture, drives the override through the one published placement and asserts only the published status codes.
